intention: Both Supercharger tables are keyed on tesla_id, account_id is gone, the mirror runs one pass per vehicle, and the gateway proves ownership before every Supercharger read.
request: MAG-67 — 4. Re-key the Supercharger pair on tesla_id; reshape the mirror. Step 4 of MAG-63.

decisions.what: tesla_id becomes NOT NULL on both Supercharger tables; account_id is dropped from both.
decisions.why: Nothing but account_id ties a supercharger_history row to an account. After the drop an orphan row (tesla_id IS NULL) is unreachable by any query, so keeping the column nullable saves nothing.

decisions.what: The migration deletes rows where tesla_id IS NULL before SET NOT NULL.
decisions.why: Owner confirmed after checking: both tables hold 0 such rows today, so the DELETE is a guard, not a data loss. The down-migration cannot restore a deleted row.

decisions.what: Run as roadmap RM57 with three tiers (telemetry, charging, gateway) instead of one standalone change.
decisions.why: Two modules each own a migration and the mirror between them is reshaped. Three smaller proposals are easier to review than one large one.

decisions.what: Tier 3 is owned by gateway; the internal/app and internal/analytics call-site updates inside it are leader-owned integration work.
decisions.why: A worker is sandboxed to one module. Port signature changes ripple into app and analytics, which is cross-module integration the leader owns by contract.

decisions.what: collectChargingHistory skips a session whose VIN is not a registered vehicle, and counts the skip in CycleReport.
decisions.why: RD1 makes tesla_id NOT NULL, so the row cannot be written. A silent skip would hide it; counting it mirrors the existing ChargingFetchFailures shape.

events.detail: RM57 from MAG-67. Branch ft/RM57-MAG-67-rekey-supercharger-pair-on-tesla-id off main 6676da8. Work counter 57 -> 58.
